newsitem.title: USA: SEC says three brokers settle kickback charges.
newsitem.headline: SEC says three brokers settle kickback charges.

text.p: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission said Monday three stockbrokers have settled the agency's charges they received kickbacks in exchange for marketing certain securities to their clients.

The SEC said the men, Robert Thomas Beatty, 55, of Hollywood, Fla., Vincent St. Clair Beatty, 34, of Parkland, Fla., and David Scott Rossman, 38, of Castlerock, Col, settled the SEC's allegations without admitting or denying any wrongdoing.

The SEC first filed suit in September 1996 in a federal court in Florida against the men and nine others alleging that some members of the group raised about $2.6 million by illegally promoted stock sales and seven of them took bribes totaling $477,580.

Based on their financial conditions, both Robert and Vincent Beatty were waived from paying $34,244 and $14,745, respectively, in civil penalties and the alleged bribe money, according to the SEC attorney handling the case.
Rossman agreed to pay a penalty and turn over his alleged bribe money, plus interest, totaling more than $8,000, according to the SEC.
The case remains open against nine other defendants and three affiliated firms.
Attorneys representing both Robert and Vincent Beatty as well as Rossman could not be reached for comment.
